text:
First decide on the parent and the numbering.

1. The carboxylic acid (-COOH) has the highest seniority, so the parent is benzoic acid and its carbon is C-1.
2. The aldehyde (-CHO) and nitrile (-CN) are stated to be meta to the ­COOH group.  In a benzoic-acid system the meta positions are C-3 and C-5.
3. The methoxy (-OCH₃) group is para (C-4) to the ­COOH group.
4. A hydroxy (-OH) and a dimethylamino (-NMe₂) are ortho to the ­COOH group, i.e. on C-2 and C-6, and the description also says that both methoxy and hydroxy are ortho to the nitrile.  That can only be true if the nitrile is at C-3 (adjacent to both C-2 and C-4).  Therefore:

   C-1  : CO₂H  
   C-2  : OH  
   C-3  : CN  
   C-4  : OMe  
   C-5  : CHO (formyl)  
   C-6  : NMe₂  

Now check which direction around the ring gives the preferred locant set.  
The two possible sets are:

• Clockwise: 2-hydroxy, 3-cyano, 4-methoxy, 5-formyl, 6-(dimethylamino) → locants 2,3,4,5,6  
• Counter-clockwise: 2-(dimethylamino), 3-formyl, 4-methoxy, 5-cyano, 6-hydroxy → locants 2,3,4,5,6  

Both give the same set of numbers, so the tie is broken by the rule that the substituent first in alphabetical order gets the lower number.  Alphabetically the first prefix is “cyano”; the clockwise numbering gives cyano the lower number (3 vs 5), so the clockwise assignment is correct.

Finally, list the substituents alphabetically in the name (ignoring multiplicative prefixes):

cyano (C) < dimethylamino (D) < formyl (F) < hydroxy (H) < methoxy (M)

Thus the correct systematic name is:

3-cyano-6-(dimethylamino)-5-formyl-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzoic acid

This matches option (C).

Answer: C
